battle.name: 高士達起義
battle.brief: 大業七年（611）冬，渤海郡人高士達聚眾於河北高雞泊，眾至數萬，攻陷郡縣，與清河張金稱等部並起，澤地同時變亂。隋將段達討之不能克，後楊義臣率遼東還兵擊破之，陣斬張金稱，入豆子澗擒格謙。卡面斯巴達長矛屬希臘工藝，不在此役現場；隋軍步卒用槊與盾成列，義軍則以符水聚民、依澤地舟船往來。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 大業七年（611）冬起於河北的一場叛亂，交戰的兩方是隋朝中央政府，與以渤海郡人高士達為首、聯合清河人張金稱、平原人孫安祖以及屯兵豆子航的劉霸道等河北澤地武裝。起事時間一般繫於大業七年冬十一月，但逐月明記的文獻有限。隋朝一方由煬帝楊廣下詔調度，先遣將軍段達率邊軍與郡兵進剿而不能克，其後詔楊義臣率遼東還兵數萬討之；義臣以檢校趙郡太守、左光祿大夫的名位統兵，兵權集中於中央調度，糧秣自太原、范陽沿官道北運，前線指揮與後方補給拉得極長。反方沒有正式名號、沒有編制、沒有固定城邑，只憑首領號召，以符水一類的民間方術聚眾，靠劫掠郡縣取得倉廩、鐵器與馬匹，部曲多為同鄉同里，靠村社結寨、依澤地水網藏身。河北平原同時湧起多支互不隸屬的義軍，彼此既互相馳援又互相爭地，沒有統一指揮系統，也沒有常備建制，人數全靠首領自報。
countriesEn: This was a rebellion that began in Hebei in the winter of Daye 7 (611). The two sides were the Sui central government on one hand, and on the other the armed bands of the Hebei marsh country led by Gao Shida, a man of Bohai Commandery, together with Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe, Sun Anzu of Pingyuan and Liu Badao, who held his ground at Douzi Hang. The outbreak is generally placed in the eleventh month of the winter of Daye 7, though the surviving record is thin on the exact month. On the Sui side the orders came from Emperor Yang of Sui, who first sent the general Duan Da with frontier troops and provincial soldiers and was then driven to commission Yang Yichen, who was to lead several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops. Yichen held the titles of Inspector of Zhao Commandery and Left Grand Master of Ceremonies; authority was centralised in the capital, grain was carried north from Taiyuan and Fangyang along the official roads, and command at the front was stretched very far from supply at the rear. The insurgents had no state name, no establishment and no fixed towns; they rallied only to the word of their chiefs, gathered followers with the sort of folk divination and healing water that circulated among the villages, and took grain, iron and horses by raiding commandery seats, their bands being made up largely of men from the same village, fortified in earthwork camps and hidden among the marshes and waterways. Several mutually independent rebel groups rose across the Hebei plain at the same time, giving each other help and fighting each other for ground, with no unified command, no standing establishment and numbers that were only ever self-reported.
people: 高士達是渤海郡人，起事時據高雞泊，即今河北衡水故城一帶的低窪鹼泊，眾至數萬，是河北義軍中最早成名的首領之一。與他同時起兵的清河人張金稱、平原人孫安祖，以及屯兵豆子航的劉霸道，就在同一片澤地與村社之間既並肩又互相爭地；河北義軍從來不是一支統一隊伍。高士達與張金稱兩部曾合兵攻涿郡而內部爭雄，張金稱死於合作破裂的餘波，舊史對具體經過只有寥寥數語，諸說並存。隋將段達最先奉詔討伐而不能克；真正扭轉局面的是關西名將楊義臣，他熟悉部眾作戰的兇悍，也熟悉河北澤地的路形，率遼東還兵數萬一舉大破之，陣中斬張金稱，隨後收合降眾編入行伍，循著降眾指路進入豆子澗，掃平另一名首領格謙。楊廣怕義臣威名過盛，急召其入朝並升授禮部尚書，義臣不久卒官，賊眾由是復盛。
peopleEn: Gao Shida was a man of Bohai Commandery, and when he rose he held the Gaoji marsh, the low salt pools lying to the south-west of modern Gucheng in Hebei. His following ran to tens of thousands, and he was one of the first rebel leaders to make a name in Hebei. Rising at the same time were Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe, Sun Anzu of Pingyuan and Liu Badao, who had his camp at Douzi Hang, all of them in the same country of marshes and villages, at once allies and rivals. The Hebei insurgents were never one army. Gao Shida and Zhang Jincheng once joined forces to attack Zhuojun and then fell to quarrelling among themselves; Zhang died in the backlash of that broken cooperation, and the old histories say only a few words about how it happened, so the accounts stand side by side. The first Sui commander, Duan Da, was sent against the rising and could not take it. The man who turned the situation was Yang Yichen, a famous general from the western marches who knew both the ferocity of steppe warfare and the tracks and water paths of the Hebei marshes. He led several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops, broke the insurgents in a single action and cut down Zhang Jincheng in the fighting; then he gathered the surrendered men into the ranks and followed their guidance into the Douzi ravine, clearing out the other leader Ge Qian. Emperor Yang, uneasy about Yichen's renown, called him abruptly to the capital and made him Minister of Rites; Yichen died in office shortly after, and the rebels grew strong again.
kits: 這張卡面畫的是斯巴達長矛（dory）：約兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套，源於公元前八世紀的希臘世界，在方陣之中靠密集的矛線決定誰站得住。它並沒有出現在河北——希臘的長槊從未越過亞洲內陸到渤海之濱，這一點必須說清楚。真正在場的是同一門工藝的另一批長柄兵器：隋軍步卒依《隋書·兵志》所載以槊為主，配盾、鑿、鉞之屬，列陣時以槊遮蔽前列、以盾承其矢，車陣之中更有以長槊構成向外翻出矛牆的卻月之陣；而河北義軍的長柄兵器更為粗獷，柄木就地取材，矛頭從鐵匠鋪與繳獲的官軍器械中得來，少有製式的鎧冑。義軍另有弓矢、符水與漁獵舟具，高雞泊一帶水面縱橫，舟船可達，步兵不利展開。同一門工藝，兩千年後在河北的鹼泊澤地遇上最不利的地形：密集長矛方陣需要平疊的正面與整齊的腳步，而泥灘、蘆葦與水面讓方陣無從排開，義軍因此先佔了便宜，隋軍最後仍是在能展開的地段靠槊兵成列而進，才把雜眾壓垮。
kitsEn: The card shows a Spartan dory: a wooden spear about two metres long with a bronze ferrule at the butt, native to the Greek world of the eighth century BC, where it decided in the phalanx who would still be standing. It was not present in Hebei: Greek long spears never travelled across the interior of Asia to the shores of the Bohai Sea, and that has to be said plainly. What was actually on the ground was another batch of long-hafted weapons of the same craft. Sui infantry, as the Weapon Treatise of the History of Sui records, fought with the suo as their principal arm, paired with shields, picks and axes, the suo masking the front rank and the shield taking the arrows, and in wagon formations there was the queyue array, its long spears opened outward into a wall of points. The long weapons of the Hebei insurgents were rougher affairs, with hafts taken from the local woods and points bought from blacksmiths or taken from captured Sui equipment, and very little plate armour of any standard. The insurgents also had bows, the healing water that drew followers, and the boats and nets of the fishing trade, for at Gaoji marsh the water lay open in every direction, boats could reach everywhere, and foot soldiers could hardly be deployed. The same craft, in the salt marshes of Hebei more than two millennia later, met the worst possible terrain: a dense spear phalanx needs a level front and disciplined footing, and mud flats, reed beds and open water gave it no line to form, so the insurgents had the advantage at first, and only on ground where the line could be opened did the Sui spear troops march in step and crush the mob.
tactics: 大業七年冬的河北，隋廷正把百餘萬人的主力壓在遼東攻高句麗，河北各郡只剩郡兵、鄉勇與臨時募集的團練，守備近乎空窗，這是義軍得以迅速聚眾、攻陷郡縣的前提。義軍的戰法大半只能從結果反推：以符水建立信眾網絡，靠人與人之間的傳播在鄉里迅速蔓延，作戰則沿用河北民間原有的自衛方式，憑村社結寨、依山澤與河渠藏身、夜間襲擾城邑與糧倉、得糧即散、官軍一到便退回鄉里。河北平原地勢開闊，官軍精騎在視野與機動上佔優，義軍若要取勝只能靠人數與多點同時爆發的混亂，故多選在郡縣守備空虛、倉廩有存、驛傳不繼的時機發動，攻陷即走，不據城、不戍守。兩家合兵攻涿郡是義軍第一次把手腳捏在一起作大手筆，卻暴露聯軍最脆弱處：攻城器械、糧秣分配與進攻次序都談不攏，圍城既久則內部互疑。隋軍這邊則是另一套路數：以少量精騎搜索、挑釁與追擊，誘使密集的義軍放箭還擊，等到對方矢石疲憊、前排擠壓成團，再以步兵持長矛列陣而前，一鼓穿透敵陣，騎兵隨即由兩翼掩殺反覆突入，直至義軍崩散；義軍的問題正在於人數雖眾而甲兵不精，弓矢一旦耗盡，密集隊形就變成長桿與刀矛的犧牲場。
tacticsEn: Hebei in the winter of Daye 7 saw the Sui court pressing more than a million men towards Liaodong against Goguryeo, so that the commanderies of Hebei were left with provincial soldiers, local levies and hastily raised auxiliaries, their defence close to empty, and that was the premise on which the insurgents could gather in crowds and overrun district seats. Their method can largely be reconstructed backwards from its results: they built a network of believers with healing water and spread it through villages by word of mouth, and in fighting they used the self-defence customs the countryside already had, fortifying in village earthworks, hiding among hills, marshes and watercourses, raiding towns and granaries by night, breaking off with the grain and returning to the villages when the government troops came. The Hebei plain is open, and the Sui cavalry held the advantage in sight and movement, so the insurgents could only win through numbers and through confusion erupting at several points at once; they therefore struck when a commandery seat was thinly held, when granaries were full and when the courier relay had been cut, and they left again as soon as they had taken it, holding no city and maintaining no garrison. The joint assault on Zhuojun was the first great thing the insurgents attempted together, and it exposed the weakest point of such a coalition: siege engines, the sharing of grain and the order of assault could not be agreed, and a prolonged siege bred suspicion. The Sui method ran the other way: a small body of cavalry searched, provoked and pursued, provoking dense masses of insurgents into shooting back until their arrows and stones were spent and their front ranks were crushed together, and then infantry with long spears marched forward in line, broke through the enemy in one push, and cavalry on the flanks rode in and out again and again until the insurgents dissolved. The weakness of the insurgents lay in the fact that their numbers were large and their armour poor: once their arrows were gone, a crowded formation became a field for long shafts and blades.
data: 關於兵數，現存記載多而確數少。《隋書·楊義臣傳》說渤海高士達與清河張金稱「相聚為盜，眾已數萬，攻陷郡縣」，又說義臣率「遼東還兵數萬」擊破之，兩處都用「數萬」一語而不給確數；河北義軍人數的舊史說法多有誇大，如「十餘萬」之類，應作概數看待。較可計數的是隋軍的總量：史載大業七年出師兵馬五十餘萬，一次用糧至一百五十萬石，往後續增至三百萬石與五百萬石，道路上的輜重與民夫遠多於作戰部隊；大業八年再出師，兵員更高。此類數字歷來被認為有所誇張，但足以說明河北與山東的丁壯被抽調一空，郡縣只剩殘兵與鄉勇。距離方面，高雞泊與豆子澗同在故城、阜城一帶，相距不過數十餘里；高雞泊至涿郡約二百餘里，義軍合兵攻涿郡的路程不遠，其在河北境內的調動多在數日之內完成。時間上，叛亂起於大業七年冬，段達不能克，義臣大破之則在大業十年前後至十二年之間，張金稱之死舊書或繫於大業十二年（616）；高士達的生死與義軍的收束在文獻上仍是懸案，諸說並存。
dataEn: On numbers, the surviving record is rich in approximations and poor in certainties. The History of Sui says of Gao Shida of Bohai and Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe that they gathered together as bandits, that their numbers had already reached tens of thousands and that they had overrun commanderies and counties, and it also says that Yichen took several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops and shattered them; both passages use the phrase several tens of thousands and give no exact figure, and the old estimates of ten-odd myriad for the Hebei insurgents are plainly rounded figures that should be read as such. The scale that can be counted better is the size of the Sui army: the chronicles give the force mustered in Daye 7 as more than half a million men, with one hundred and fifty thousand shi of grain for the first provisioning, later raised to three hundred thousand and then to five hundred thousand, the carts and the labour gangs on the roads far outnumbering the troops who fought, and the next campaign of Daye 8 was larger still. Such figures are generally held to be exaggerated, but they are enough to show the men of Hebei and Shandong being stripped away until the commanderies had nothing left but remnants and local levies. As for distances: the Gaoji marsh and the Douzi ravine lie within a few tens of li of one another around Gucheng and Fucheng, and from Gaoji to Zhuojun is a little over two hundred li, so the joint march on Zhuojun was no long journey, and the insurgents moved about inside Hebei within days. In time, the rising began in the winter of Daye 7; Duan Da could not take it; Yichen's crushing of it fell somewhere between the years Daye 10 and Daye 12, and the old books place Zhang Jincheng's death in Daye 12 (616). The fate of Gao Shida himself, and the closing of the rising, remain a suspended question in the literature, and the accounts stand side by side.
cause: 打起來的直接起因是役繁加災荒。大業七年隋煬帝再征高句麗，天下丁壯按戶徵發，河北與山東出丁最多；渤海郡與信都一帶連年水旱，農田絕收，倉廩為空，縣吏卻仍嚴催服遼東兵役，鄉民無以為生。第二環是權力結構的鬆動：隋朝把主力百餘萬人推往遼東，河北只剩郡兵與鄉勇，郡縣守備近乎空窗，鄉里宗族、地方豪強與散兵游勇遂各自成為武裝核心，高士達、張金稱、孫安祖、劉霸道皆出於此類社會層。第三環是義軍之間的競爭與互相消耗：高雞泊、豆子航與清河、易縣各聚數萬眾，義軍既互相馳援，也爭奪糧道與地盤，張金稱與高士達兩部最後的合作破裂，把本來分散的起義捲入內鬥。第四環是隋廷的反應失序：煬帝遠在涿郡與江都之間巡遊，河北的清剿分散歸各郡自行處理，既無統一指揮，也無長期部署，義軍得以在澤地與村落之間蔓延十年。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the fighting was heavy service combined with crop failure. In Daye 7 Emperor Yang mustered for another war against Goguryeo and took the able-bodied men of every household, and Hebei and Shandong gave more of them than any other province. Around Bohai Commandery and Xindu there were successive floods and droughts, the fields yielded nothing, the granaries stood empty, and the county officials still pressed the men into service for the Liaodong armies, so that the villages had no way to live. The second link is the loosening of the structure of power: the court pushed more than a million men towards Liaodong, leaving Hebei with provincial soldiers and local levies and the commanderies close to empty, so that village clans, local strongmen and stray soldiers each became a nucleus of armed force, and Gao Shida, Zhang Jincheng, Sun Anzu and Liu Badao all came out of exactly that layer of society. The third link is the competition between the insurgents, which consumed them in turn: tens of thousands gathered at the Gaoji marsh, at Douzi Hang, in Qinghe and around Yi County, giving each other help and at the same time fighting over grain roads and ground, until the cooperation of Zhang Jincheng and Gao Shida broke down and drew a scattered rebellion into civil war. The fourth link is the disorder of the court's response: with Yang Guang away at Zhuojun and Jiangdu, the suppression in Hebei was left to each commandery to handle on its own, with no unified command and no long-term plan, and the insurgents could spread through the marshes and villages for a decade.
impact: 這場起義的第一重後果，是隋朝在河北的秩序被打穿一個大洞。渤海郡、博陵、涿郡、清河一線的郡縣數年之後仍攻守不定，義軍與官軍在澤地、村社與道路之間拉鋸，隋廷必須從遼東與關中抽調兵將回援，結果是前方的高句麗戰役更無力支撐——大業八年與九年的兩次深入都沒有拿下平壤，高句麗得以延續其政權。第二重後果在制度層面：隋廷以「討賊」為名把兵權散給諸王，煬帝令子弟分鎮諸州，以防地方再叛，這種封王鎮州的做法在隋末迅速演成割據的溫床。第三重後果在河北的權力結構：義軍首領之間的吞併與內鬥，把散兵游勇、鄉里武裝與流亡戶一併推入竇建德麾下，河北義軍由多頭並起轉為一家獨大，而竇建德一部自大業七年冬季的鄉里數百人，到隋亡時號稱數十萬、控制的城池以十數計。第四重後果在北方：河北與山東的亂民、散卒大量北流，流入遼東與渤海、靺鞨、契丹各部，隋末東北亂局的最後一波由此成形，隋朝失其東北，遼東的秩序要等到唐初才重新建立起來。
impactEn: The first consequence of this rising was a hole torn in the order of the Sui in Hebei. The commanderies along Bohai, Boling, Zhuojun and Qinghe remained insecure for years afterwards, insurgents and government troops tugging at each other between the marshes, the villages and the roads, and the court had to recall generals and soldiers from Liaodong and from the Guanzhong basin, which left the war against Goguryeo even less supported: neither the campaign of Daye 8 nor that of Daye 9 brought Pyongyang down, and Goguryeo went on living. The second consequence was institutional: under the pretext of suppressing bandits the court dispersed military power to the princes, and Yang Guang sent his sons to hold the various prefectures so that no district might rebel again, and what was meant as a remedy hardened into the breeding ground of the warlordism that marked the end of the Sui. The third consequence fell on the structure of power in Hebei itself: as the rebel leaders swallowed one another and fought among themselves, they pushed stray soldiers, village bands and fugitives alike into the following of Dou Jiande, and a rebellion that had begun with many heads came under a single one, while Dou's own band grew from a few hundred men from one village in the winter of Daye 7 to a force claiming tens of thousands and holding a dozen or more cities by the time the Sui fell. The fourth consequence lay to the north: displaced people and scattered soldiers from Hebei and Shandong moved north in great numbers, into Liaodong and into the Bohai, Mohe and Khitan peoples, and the last wave of disorder in the north-east of the late Sui took shape from that movement, so that the Sui lost its north-east and the order of Liaodong had to wait for the early Tang to build it again.
result: 結局分兩層。就戰役本身：段達首討不能克，高士達眾至數萬、攻陷郡縣，張金稱被斬，格謙於豆子澗被擒，楊義臣以遼東還兵數萬大破叛軍主力，隋廷在戰術上贏了這一仗。然而楊廣怕義臣威名過盛，急召其入朝、升任禮部尚書，叛軍隨即復盛；這說明這場戰爭並未真正結束——一次會戰的勝利替代不了對郡縣的治理，也替代不了對澤地流民的安撫。高士達本人的下落則史無明文：《隋書》只記義臣「大破士達」，並未言其被擒被斬與生死，故此役的收束在文獻上是懸案，諸說並存；另據一系記載，河北高士達後為張須陀於河間所破，部眾歸竇建德，與《隋書》楊義臣傳所記義臣斬金稱、擒格謙者，先後與成敗互有出入，兩說並存，難以斷其是非。往後看，河北義軍的力量在消耗與吞併中逐漸歸於一家，隋朝在起義的連續消耗之下於大業十四年（618）崩潰，長江以北盡成群雄割據之勢。河北這片土地在隋唐之際的結局，可以說是隋朝失其河北，而新的河北秩序要等到唐朝才重新建立起來。
resultEn: The outcome has two layers. As a campaign: the first Sui commander, Duan Da, could not take the rising; Gao Shida's host had run to tens of thousands and had overrun commanderies and counties; Zhang Jincheng was cut down; Ge Qian was taken alive in the Douzi ravine; and Yang Yichen, with several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops, shattered the main body of the insurgents, so that the court won this battle on the field. Yet Emperor Yang, fearing Yichen's renown, called him abruptly to the capital and made him Minister of Rites, and the insurgents rose again at once, which shows the war had not really been ended, because one victory in the field could replace neither the government of the commanderies nor the pacification of the displaced in the marshes. Gao Shida's own fate is nowhere recorded: the History of Sui says only that Yichen broke him badly, without saying whether he was taken, killed or survived, so the closing of this rising is a suspended question in the literature and the accounts stand side by side. Another line of record has Gao Shida of Hebei broken later by Zhang Xutuo at Hejian, his men going over to Dou Jiande; between that and what the History of Sui says in the biography of Yichen, about the cutting down of Zhang Jincheng and the taking of Ge Qian, the order and the outcome do not agree, and the two cannot be settled. Looking further ahead, the rebel forces in Hebei were gradually spent and swallowed up until they came under a single head, and the Sui, worn down by one rising after another, collapsed in Daye 14 (618), leaving everything north of the Yangtze in the hands of contending warlords. The end of the story in Hebei across the Sui-Tang hinge is that the Sui lost Hebei, and a new order for that province had to wait for the Tang to build it again.
